long_biography.plain_text:
William Samuel Hugh 'Sam' Laidlaw grew up with the energy industry close at hand: his father became BP's deputy chairman, and school trips included refineries. After Eton, Cambridge law and INSEAD, he spent two decades at Amerada Hess, building its North Sea business before becoming president and chief operating officer. He later led Enterprise Oil through a sale to Shell and joined Chevron as an executive vice-president.

At Centrica, Laidlaw directed a utility spanning household energy, power generation and upstream production through eight years of intense political and market scrutiny. After leaving in 2014, he created Neptune Energy with backing from Carlyle and CVC. The platform acquired Engie's international exploration and production business and developed a gas-oriented portfolio across Europe, North Africa and Asia.

At Centrica, Laidlaw directed a utility spanning household energy, power generation and upstream production through eight years of intense political and market scrutiny. After leaving in 2014, he created Neptune Energy with backing from Carlyle and CVC. The platform acquired Engie's international exploration and production business and developed a gas-oriented portfolio across Europe, North Africa and Asia.
